title: perf(canary): add automated latency/throughput regression detector and rollout guards
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds an automated performance canary detector that triggers rollout guards on latency or throughput regressions. Backwards-compatible, enabled behind feature flag.
description: Context: We've seen several incidents where canary rollouts failed to detect subtle latency regressions caused by batching and KV cache interactions. This PR adds a continuous perf canary detector that compares live canary traffic against baseline models and triggers rollout guards when regression signals exceed configured thresholds. Motivation: Reduce noisy manual reviews and avoid large rollouts that increase user latency/cost. This change implements automated detection for P50/P95 latency regressions, throughput regressions, kv-cache-hit-rate drops, and request-size distribution shifts. Design: 1) Detector service: new perf_canary/detector that ingests canary and baseline time-series (latency, throughput, kv_hit, batch_size) and computes rolling-window statistical tests (bootstrap CI on P95, relative throughput ratios). 2) Threshold profiles: per-model configurable thresholds with hysteresis and cooldown windows to avoid flapping. Profiles live in runtime-config and are overrideable per-deploy. 3) Rollout guards: when detector reports a regression above threshold for longer than N minutes, the rollout engine automatically pauses or aborts the canary and triggers configured fallback actions (rollback, reduce traffic, notify). 4) Observability: added metrics (perf_canary.regression_count, perf_canary.hysteresis_state, perf_canary.cooldown_seconds) and tracing hooks that annotate canary traces. 5) Feature gating: new feature flag enable_perf_canary_auto_detect controls behavior; default off for early rollouts. Implementation highlights: - New detector binary (perf_canary/detector.go) with a lightweight in-memory windowed aggregator and an adapter to the existing metrics pipeline. - Added rollout guard integration (services/rollout/guard.go) that accepts detector signals and applies hysteresis logic. - Extended canary config schema to include thresholds, hysteresis_period, cooldown_period, and kv_hit_weight. - Unit + integration tests for detection logic and guard transitions, plus a perf test harness that runs synthetic canary traffic against a baseline to validate sensitivity. Testing and CI: - Local unit tests and integration tests added. - End-to-end perf canary job runs as part of ci/perf-canary pipeline; synthetic workloads validated against a baseline commit. - CI initially flagged flaky e2e due to a timing assumption; fixed retry logic and increased windowing for stability. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable for internal 'perf' team canaries for 2 weeks (monitor metrics). 3) Gradual enablement for production canaries with conservative thresholds and long hysteresis. Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation - [x] Rollout guard integration - [x] Config schema migration - [x] Tests (unit/integration/e2e) - [x] Docs: added runtime-config and rollout guide - [x] Observability dashboards updated Notes/Limitations: - Detector uses aggregated metrics rather than per-request full traces for performance; this keeps it lightweight but may miss very low-signal regressions. - Threshold tuning will be iterative; initial profiles use conservative defaults. Related: ENG-8732 (perf canary design), ENG-8801 (rollout guard requirements), SUP-1245 (customer incident that motivated hysteresis).
